definitions.meaning: slips are mistakes or howlers, informally called boobs or gaffes
old-fashioned baggy knickers made by makers of underwear

explanation.surface: Petticoats coming off the production line at an underwear factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slips' looks like the underwear item, which suits the lingerie picture, but it means errors.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: a blunder is a bloomer, and so are loose old-style knickers sold by underwear firms.

definitions.meaning: to strike repeatedly, as wind strikes a ship
a self-service spread of food set out by caterers

explanation.surface: A walkout arranged by kitchen workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests industrial action, which fits the catering staff, but it means to batter.
explanation.definitionFit: Waves batter or knock a boat about; a spread of food laid out for guests to help themselves.

parts.note: O looks like a zero, nothing
to rate is to reckon or count, so counts means rates

explanation.surface: Someone voices an opinion, though it matters not at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Declaims, making a formal speech in public.

clue.text: Rather wet? One's among the majority!

indicators.note: among says one piece sits within the other

parts.note: most means the majority
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: A remark that someone counts among the larger group.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly damp, a little wet.

explanation.surface: Freed, and freed again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into re- (again) and lease (rent out).
explanation.definitionFit: Freeing a prisoner; and leasing a property once more, renting it out a second time.

clue.text: Contrive to allow a guy time

parts.note: a guy is a man
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A request to give some fellow a little more time.
explanation.definitionFit: To contrive to do something is to succeed in doing it despite difficulty, a synonym.

clue.text: Top to bottom, an unexpected calamity

definitions.text: Top to bottom, an unexpected calamity

parts.words: Top to bottom, an unexpected calamity
parts.note: a sudden disaster that sweeps from the summit of a mountain down to its foot

explanation.surface: A disaster that strikes suddenly from end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass of snow sliding from a mountain's peak to its base is a sudden disaster.

clue.text: Publicises tour for down-to earth travellers

parts.note: to air views is to publicise them
a trip is a tour

explanation.surface: Advertises a holiday for unpretentious, practical people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down-to earth' looks like sensible, but means flyers coming down to land.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of land where light aircraft land, bringing flyers down to the ground.

indicators.note: orders suggests putting the letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An officer's commands to inflate or demolish something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orders' rearranges GENERALS; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow up a photograph is to make it bigger.

clue.text: Feel bias of some sort? Quite likely

indicators.note: of some sort suggests these letters in some other form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wondering whether one has a kind of prejudice, which seems probable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of some sort' rearranges the eight letters of FEEL BIAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that could well happen or be done is plausible or practicable, a looser synonym.

parts.note: reads as the partner of comedian Oliver Hardy, but also a tough evergreen shrub that survives frost

explanation.surface: Naming the comic partner of Oliver Hardy in the famous film double act.
explanation.walkthrough: Stan and Ollie were the comedy duo; 'Hardy' also means frost-resistant, as gardeners say of plants.
explanation.definitionFit: The bay tree is a frost-resistant evergreen, and Stan was the comic partner of Oliver Hardy.

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of an Asian country's money from the past.
explanation.walkthrough: The coin was a sixteenth of a rupee in former Indian currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A former Indian coin worth one sixteenth of a rupee.

clue.text: Regards discipline as a personal problem

parts.note: to regard is to look at, so regards means eyes as a verb
to discipline is to train

explanation.surface: Someone treating self-control as their own private difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired, aching vision from overuse is an individual ailment.

parts.note: bird and stir are both slang for a prison sentence or prison

explanation.surface: Someone woke a bird up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' is not a feathered creature here: in British slang 'doing bird' and 'in stir' both mean being in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up and moving about, awake and active, is the state of having been roused.

indicators.note: fed-up hints at turning upside down, so the run is read backwards
from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone quits a post, definitely sick of the options.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' picks EDEC out of the end of choicE and start of DECidedly; 'fed-up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up or surrender a position is to relinquish it, a synonym.

parts.note: to insert data is to enter it

indicators.note: include says the can wraps around the a

parts.note: a can is a tin

explanation.surface: Advertising material inserts may come with a presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: To host guests is to receive them and look after them, a synonym.

parts.note: a scribe is a writer or copyist

explanation.surface: An author will be given acknowledgement for their work.
explanation.definitionFit: To attribute something to a person is to give them credit for it.

indicators.note: alternative suggests another arrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: A drinker is offered just one glass and no other choice.
explanation.definitionFit: On condition that, the phrase used to set a single requirement.

parts.note: reads as rising after a lie-in, but means digging up the late, the dead

explanation.surface: Advice to have a lie-in before rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' means dead, so this is exhuming a body, not oversleeping.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhume is to dig a buried body out of the ground.

clue.text: Given direction, coloured and made economies

parts.note: S is south, a compass direction
tinted means coloured

explanation.surface: Someone told which way to go, dyed something, and saved money.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp, holding back on spending, is to economise.

definitions.meaning: to treat with something is to handle it

explanation.surface: Applying preservative to a piece of soft timber.
explanation.definitionFit: To handle a problem; and fir or pine boards as timber.

definitions.meaning: matelots are sailors, the people who man a ship
crowed, of which an old past tense is the same word as the sailors

explanation.surface: Sailors bragging that they were better than everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: Matelot is British slang for a sailor; the cock crew is an old past tense of crow.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's company of sailors is its complement; and an archaic past tense of crow means bragged.

clue.text: Cole-not the merry old king, a dull fellow

definitions.meaning: cole is a brassica, the green vegetable, not Old King Cole of the nursery rhyme
a slang term for a dreary, inactive person

explanation.surface: Insisting someone called Cole is a bore, not the jolly monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Old King Cole is the merry old soul of an English nursery rhyme; cole is also kale or similar greens.
explanation.definitionFit: Cole is a leafy green vegetable; and a listless, inert person is likened to a vegetable.

indicators.note: perplexity suggests confusion, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Showing bafflement without saying a word.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign up or join, as for military service, is to enrol.

clue.text: Came together to find greed destroying a great number at first

indicators.note: at first says this piece goes before the rest

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a great number

indicators.note: destroying suggests the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: People meeting and finding that avarice ruined a crowd early on.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'a great number' as a crowd, but it is the Roman numeral for a thousand; 'at first' puts it ahead of the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that combined into one have fused or joined.

definitions.note: the clue's adjective points to the noun for a kind of willow

indicators.note: form says the letters are moulded into a new shape

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Rosie has a slender, graceful figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' rearranges ROSIE; the possessive gives no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a willow tree whose pliant shoots are used in basket-making.

clue.text: A person must be patient using such transport

definitions.text: A person must be patient using such transport

parts.words: A person must be patient using such transport
parts.note: patient looks like an adjective about waiting, but the rider is a sick person being carried to hospital

explanation.surface: A warning that this form of travel requires plenty of patience.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergency vehicles carry sick or injured people, the patients, to hospital.

clue.text: Came down on a man for being flexible

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed after, below the first piece

parts.note: a bird that lit came down to land
he refers to a man

explanation.surface: Someone landed on a man for being too pliable.
explanation.definitionFit: Supple and agile, bending easily.

clue.text: Procured some meat in Batman's city

parts.note: procured means got
ham is a kind of meat

explanation.surface: A shopping trip to buy a little meat in the superhero's home town.
explanation.definitionFit: The comic-book hero guards a fictional city that is a stand-in for New York.

clue.text: Out-of-reach item when there's very little money

parts.note: something out of reach is far away
an item is a thing

explanation.surface: Some object one cannot reach at a time when funds are low.
explanation.walkthrough: The coin was a quarter of an old British penny, so it stands for almost no money.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarter-penny coin was the smallest sum in old British currency, so idiomatically a tiny amount.

clue.text: The way to call for a tie-up

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
to ring is to call on the telephone

explanation.surface: Instructions on how to phone to arrange a business link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cord or twine is what you use to tie something up.

clue.text: Beaten by one deed inside another

indicators.note: inside says the first deed sits within the second

parts.note: another deed, given as the word deed itself
a feat is a deed, especially a bold one

explanation.surface: Overcome by one act tucked inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Being overcome in a contest means losing, a synonym.
